text:
Adam Fox has 24 points in 22 games, 22 of them assists, and our numbers say he has been shortchanged. The Rangers have scored 5.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That usually swings back, and his points would swing with it.

The play driving is the story. New York controls 60.2% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at 5v5 when Fox is out there, 10.8 points better than when he sits. He is playing more, too: 24.4 minutes a night over his last ten, up from earlier in the season. Over that stretch the Rangers won six of seven.

Evolving-Hockey's model rated him ninth among 215 defensemen last season, and unusually for an offensive star, most of his value came from defense: opponents got fewer quality chances with him on the ice, 94th percentile. He is no burner and his shot is light (18th percentile in top speed); he wins with reads. A Norris winner at 23, he is 28 now and on a pace in our range near 83 points. The goals have been slow. The rest is there.
headline: Fox is better than his points say
